answer: Randomness-Gated Role Assignment. Each epoch a public verifiable random function assigns agents to roles; only assigned agents may transact, and assignment requires a valid credential bound to a prior epoch's seed. An attacker cannot precompute which of their clones get roles, so most sit idle. Registering N identities costs N full epochs of upkeep plus credentials for expected yield of one role, making marginal sybil cost exceed single-agent profit. A fable of infinite clones fails here; each willow branch needs its own credential. The atlas of roles stays fixed while costs scale linearly.
